newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil won't change CVRD selloff plan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil won't change CVRD selloff plan.

text.p: The Brazilian government does not intend to change its proposed model for the privatization of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), a Planning Minstry spokesman said.
A proposal by the president of the Chamber of Deputies Luiz Eduardo Magalhaes, that the company be sold entirely via public offering, was unacceptable, the spokesman said.
"That was never the government's idea and the government won't alter its model," he said.

The government plans to privatize CVRD in the first quarter of 1997 with a 40-45 percent block sale of voting shares, followed by a sale of further shares to employees and a global offering later in 1997.

That plan was questioned by Magalhaes who on Sunday handed President Fernando Henrique Cardoso an alternative proposal that CVRD be sold entirely by public offering along the lines of privatizations carried out by the British government.

Planning Minister Antonio Kandir believes this would reduce by one billion reais the government's receipts from the sale of its shares in CVRD, worth an estimated five and six billion reais, the spokesman said.

The spokesman also said the minimum price of the 40-45 percent block and tender details for its sale would not be announced at a December 18 meeting of the National Privatization Council as had been expected.
Those details would probably be made public after the council's January meeting, he said.
The Brazilian government on Wednesday said the block sale of CVRD's voting shares would probably take place in March, dousing market hopes of a February start to the privatization.
